candidate.claim: For post-selection inference over already-valid e-confidence intervals, e-BY controls false coverage rate under arbitrary dependence and arbitrary selection, and can be used with stopped confidence sequences; real Twitter A/B data show tighter/faster decisions than BY in the studied setup.

primary_source.title: Post-selection inference for e-value based confidence intervals

theorem.procedure: For selected set S among K parameters, e-BY sets alpha_i = delta*|S|/K for each selected i.
theorem.guarantee: Theorem 2 states FCR <= delta for any dependence structure among X_1,...,X_K and any selection rule, provided each supplied C_i(alpha) is a valid e-CI for all alpha.
theorem.key_precondition: The arbitrary-dependence/selection guarantee starts after marginal e-CI validity has been established; e-BY does not construct validity for a misspecified marginal process.

sequential_scope.detail: The paper explicitly develops e-CIs from stopped confidence sequences/e-processes and notes applicability at stopping times, continuously monitored confidence sequences and bandit sampling.
sequential_scope.clarification: Stopping-time validity is relative to the filtration and assumptions under which the underlying confidence sequence/e-process is valid; e-BY does not repair a confidence sequence invalidated by an incorrect dependence/filtration model.

twitter_AB_application.dataset: 263 Twitter A/B experiments over 1.5 years, each run at least two weeks; 15 metrics, treated as K=30 control/treatment parameters, observed daily.
twitter_AB_application.selection_rule: same simplified shipping criteria for both procedures; e-BY shippable set is a strict superset in the reported comparison
twitter_AB_application.important_precision_scope: The application uses an asymptotic confidence sequence from Waudby-Smith et al.; the paper argues first-day samples are on the order of 10^6 users so the boundary is close to the true CS boundary. Therefore the Twitter numbers are practical/asymptotic empirical evidence, not a standalone exact finite-sample demonstration of e-BY's theorem.

simulation_scope.detail: The paper includes bounded and stopped-Brownian-motion simulations across varying K/dependence/signal settings to compare FCR/tightness; the current audit did not independently re-extract every simulation grid value because the O_FEED claim relies primarily on the theorem and Twitter headline results.

scope_clarifications: Theorem 2 is post-selection FCR control, not family-wise coverage and not per-selected-interval conditional coverage.

Arbitrary dependence applies among the already-valid e-CIs/data components; it must not be paraphrased as permission to choose an invalid task/cluster/dependence model on the same data and expect e-BY to repair it.
FCR may not be the appropriate loss for a single high-stakes binary deployment gate; the theorem supports a family of selected interval statements under its stated error criterion.
The Twitter comparison is not a randomized comparison of production decisions between procedures; it is a retrospective replay using one team's simplified shipping criteria on the same dataset.
The 1.2 vs 1.5 day average is computed only over experiments for which BY (and therefore e-BY) eventually satisfies shipping criteria, not over all 263 experiments.

The Twitter marginal intervals are asymptotic CSes, so avoid calling the 127/122 and 1.2/1.5 figures an exact finite-sample certificate even though the e-BY theorem itself is exact conditional on valid e-CIs.
confidence: high for Theorem 2, sequential applicability and reported Twitter figures; no independent replay of Twitter data performed
unresolved: Post-selection-valid procedures when the analyst adaptively chooses among competing dependence/clustering models using the same data.
Agent-specific family definitions and whether FCR is the right objective for a small number of high-stakes mechanism accept/reject decisions.
Exact finite-sample agent-evaluation demonstrations combining valid task/cluster-aware e-processes with post-selection e-BY.
downstream_instruction: Retain e-BY as a post-selection layer only after marginal e-CI/e-process validity is established. Keep the Twitter 127-vs-122 and 1.2-vs-1.5-day results labeled as retrospective application with asymptotic CSes and common-subset timing, not exact finite-sample agent-evaluation evidence.
